title: Free profinite internal Hom evaluated on arbitrary injective resolutions
statement:
Work on the small coherent profinite site of [def-weil-size-convention], whose coverings are finite jointly surjective families, in the compatible coefficient universes there. Use internal modules over a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with sheafified abelian tensor [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] and ordinary derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $A$ be any such commutative condensed ring, and let $E_A$ be the internal-to-sectionwise module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Write $A_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for its sheaf of section rings. Internal $A$-modules form a Grothendieck abelian category and admit nonnegative injective resolutions. The equivalence $E_A$ is exact, preserves injectives, and identifies internal tensor and its Hom right adjoint with sectionwise module tensor and slice sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For a profinite set $P$, let $A[P]$ be the free internal module on $S\mapsto C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction] and set $H_P(N)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[P],N)$. There are additive isomorphisms
$$H_P(N)(S)\cong N(S\times P),$$
natural in the module $N$ and in both profinite variables. Here $A(S)$ acts on the right through restriction along $S\times P\to S$. The isomorphism is evaluation on the tautological free generator over $S\times P$. Under it, restriction along $u:S'\to S$ is $N(u\times1_P)$, and precomposition with $A[v]:A[P']\to A[P]$ for $v:P'\to P$ is $N(1_S\times v)$.
For every internal module $M$ and every nonnegative injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$, the complex $J^\bullet=H_P(I^\bullet)$ represents $RH_P(M[0])$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. Evaluation gives $J^n(S)=I^n(S\times P)$, with differential $d_{I^\bullet}(S\times P)$. The augmentation $H_P(M)[0]\to J^\bullet$ evaluates to $M(S\times P)[0]\to I^\bullet(S\times P)$ induced by the given resolution. All these identifications commute with maps of resolutions and the two displayed restriction operations. No acyclicity of $M$ on profinite objects or projectivity of $A[P]$ is asserted.

proof.text: The profinite representables are sheaves: for a finite jointly surjective covering of $T$, put $q:\coprod T_i\to T$. This is a compact-Hausdorff surjection, hence a quotient map by [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient]. Compatible continuous maps $T_i\to P$ descend uniquely as set maps along $q$, and continuity follows from its quotient property. The empty covering of the empty object also satisfies this assertion. Products are the usual finite products of profinite spaces, so $h_S\times h_P=h_{S\times P}$. The size convention makes this a small ringed site. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] to $A_{\rm sec}$. The equivalence $E_A$ of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and preservation of limits and colimits by equivalences [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] transport its generator, colimits and exact filtered colimits to internal modules. Thus these are Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], embed $M$ into $I^0$, its cokernel into $I^1$, and each successive cokernel into the next injective. The differentials are quotient followed by embedding; their kernels are the preceding images. With zero terms in negative degrees this is a nonnegative injective resolution.

source.place: Tag 07A5, section-unbounded, opening paragraph; compact quotient descent and successive-cokernel resolution construction written here

proof.text: By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E_A$ is exact and identifies relative tensors by the map that is the identity on local pure tensors. It preserves injectives: a lifting problem into $E_A(I)$ along a monomorphism transports through the inverse exact equivalence to a lifting problem into $I$, and a lift transports back. The internal Hom $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(K,-)$ is right adjoint to $K\otimes_A-$ by [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]. The tensor/Hom adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] therefore identifies $E_A\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(K,N)$ with $\mathcal Hom_{A_{\rm sec}}(E_AK,E_AN)$: their Hom sets from $E_AL$ both equal $\operatorname{Hom}_A(K\otimes_A L,N)$, naturally in $L$. The representing isomorphism carries evaluation to evaluation, because both evaluations correspond to the identity under this bijection. This also fixes the normalization of the transported Hom.

source.place: Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor; transport by the pure-tensor comparison

proof.text:
For any internal module $B$, the free adjunction [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction] and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give $B(S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[h_S],B)$, by evaluation at $[1_S]$. Apply this to $B=H_P(N)$. Use the Hom adjunction from step 2 and the generator-preserving tensor isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] to obtain
$$H_P(N)(S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[h_S]\otimes_A A[h_P],N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[h_{S\times P}],N)\cong N(S\times P).$$
For $m\in N(S\times P)$, the associated tensor map sends a local generator $[s]\otimes[p]$ over $T$, with $s:T\to S$ and $p:T\to P$, to $N((s,p))(m)$. Conversely, if $x\in H_P(N)(S)$, pull $x$ to $S\times P$ along $\mathrm{pr}_S$ and evaluate it on $[\mathrm{pr}_P]$. These maps are inverse: this last evaluation recovers $m$, and all other values follow by restriction along $(s,p)$ and linear extension. Equality on generalized generators detects equality by the cited linearization node. Addition commutes with these formulas; multiplying $x$ by $a\in A(S)$ multiplies its value by $A(\mathrm{pr}_S)(a)$. Thus the bijection is additive and has the asserted scalar action.

source.place: Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor, combined with free linearization and Yoneda; explicit generator computation

proof.text: In the formula of step 3, replacing $x$ by its restriction along $u:S'\to S$ replaces $s:T\to S'$ by $u\circ s$. Hence it sends $m$ to $N(u\times1_P)(m)$. Precomposition with $A[v]$, for $v:P'\to P$, replaces the generator $[p']$ by $[v\circ p']$ and sends $m$ to $N(1_S\times v)(m)$. Finally a module map $b:N\to N'$ gives $b_TN((s,p))(m)=N'((s,p))b_{S\times P}(m)$. These identities prove naturality in all three variables, including mixed compositions, because $(u\times1)\circ(1\times v)=(1\times v)\circ(u\times1)$ with the corresponding sources and targets.

source.place: Paragraph (3), profinite-parameter input; naturality calculation on the generators of step 3

proof.text:
The functor $H_P$ is additive by the bilinear evaluation formula in step 3; it is left exact as the right adjoint of tensor from step 2. By [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] and step 1 every complex in internal modules admits a K-injective resolution, so [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] supplies $RH_P$ and its computation comparison on K-injectives. Any given nonnegative injective resolution $M[0]\to I^\bullet$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Consequently the canonical derived computation is
$$RH_P(M[0])\cong H_P(I^\bullet).$$
Its augmentation is degreewise application of $H_P$ to $M[0]\to I^\bullet$, followed by localization, exactly as in the computation unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. This derives $H_P$ only in its module variable.

Apply steps 3–4 to every $I^n$ and to $d_I^n:I^n\to I^{n+1}$. They identify $J^n(S)$ with $I^n(S\times P)$ and $d_J^n(S)$ with $d_I^n(S\times P)$. Applying the same calculation to the resolution augmentation identifies its degree-zero map with $M(S\times P)\to I^0(S\times P)$ and its other terms with zero. For a chain map $b^\bullet:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$, its component becomes $b^n(S\times P)$, and the chain identity remains $d_{I'}^n b^n=b^{n+1}d_I^n$ evaluated at $S\times P$. The formulas of step 4 commute with each such component and with the augmentations, proving all the claimed compatibilities as identifications of complexes and hence of their derived objects.
